THURSDAY 24 SEPTEMBER 2026 FRONT PAGES (Sky News "The Wrap" round-up)

THE TIMES (17:36): "The Conservatives have announced plans to cut benefits for the long-term unemployed, reports The Times."

DAILY TELEGRAPH (16:55): "Kemi Badenoch has set out plans to prevent unemployed people from spending their benefits money on alcohol, cigarettes and gambling, writes The Daily Telegraph."

THE GUARDIAN (17:15): "In a 'radical' shake-up of the school system, teenagers will be offered a range of new vocational GCSEs as the government looks to tackle the number of young people not in work, education or training, reports The Guardian."

FINANCIAL TIMES (16:36): "Chancellor John Healey is considering a smaller fiscal buffer in a bid to reduce tax rises in his first budget next month, according to the Financial Times."

THE I PAPER (16:48): "The i Paper reports that a senior EU figure has urged Andy Burnham to drop the government's 'obsolete' Brexit red lines to allow for a much deeper agreement with the bloc."

DAILY MIRROR (17:11): "Two RAF pilots ejected from a plane just moments before the aircraft crashed, writes the Daily Mirror." [outlet not approved — story corroborated by BBC/Sky]

THE SUN (17:08): PM says ban on drinking alcohol in football stands could be scrapped. [outlet not approved]
DAILY MAIL (17:19): Badenoch "ruthless crackdown" on benefits bill. [outlet not approved]
DAILY EXPRESS (16:34): Badenoch vows to cut benefits for those deemed not to have paid enough tax. [outlet not approved]
DAILY STAR (16:44): Jeremy Clarkson sheep miscount. [outlet not approved]
METRO (16:30): "Wolf of Essex" conman jailed for £1.3m Ponzi scheme. [outlet not approved]

SUMMARY: The Thursday front pages split three ways — Badenoch's benefits crackdown (Times, Telegraph, Mail, Express), the vocational GCSE shake-up (Guardian), and Healey's Budget fiscal buffer (FT). The i leads on EU pressure over Brexit red lines.
